messages:
lauren: FYI 1: new consultant/vendor classification + emergency spend flow now live. This changes approval matrix for consultants and creates a 24h procurement fast-track for security or incident-driven purchases. Read below and use the correct intake form. :rotating_light:

rafael: short version: consultants now have Class A/B/C based on access & contract risk. Class A = high-sensitivity (infra/SRE/production access) requires VP finance sign-off; Class B = standard consultants require L2 manager + procurement; Class C = low-risk (short-term advisory, no infra access) can be pre-approved up to $10k by procurement.

priya: Q: how do we classify an external contractor doing model evals? model evals touch data but not infra. is that A or B?

alex: For model evals that touch production data we treat as Class A. If it's synthetic / sandbox only, Class B. When in doubt, tag as A and procurement will confirm.

lauren: New intake link: https://confluence.redwood/proc/intake (please use the dropdown for 'Consultant Classification'). Template snippet below for email/ticket. Also GL mapping guidance included.

proc-bot: Intake form submitted: PRC-981 by alex 1: status: intake received, classification pending.

lauren: Emergency spend notes: if a security incident or production outage requires rapid vendor/contractor work, file an Emergency Procurement Request (EPR) with subject `EPR: <team> - <brief>` and tag @procurement and @security. Procurement aims to respond within 4 business hours for EPRs under $75k. For >$75k we'll escalate but can provision provisional PO within 24h where possible.

rafael: Please include minimal required fields for EPR: incident ticket link, business impact, estimated spend, vendor contact + bank details, and whether the vendor needs immediate infra access. Example subject: `EPR: infra-team - incident-1142`.

priya: Do we still need three quotes for >$25k on EPRs? that can slow things down for security hires.

proc-bot: Policy note: For EPRs, the 3-quote rule is waived for time-sensitive security/incident work, but procurement will do post-hoc vendor review and documented justification is required.

emma: GL codes reminded: contractors/consulting = 5102, security/incident remediation = 6207, cloud infra = 6003. If you need help mapping correct GL, drop to #finance-help and include the intake ID.

alex: small procedural thing 1: if the consultant requires access to production or PII, security must sign-off before procurement issues PO. This is non-negotiable.

lauren: We'll publish the updated procurement matrix and a one-page quick guide in Confluence by EOD. We'll also run two office hours this week (Wed 11am PT, Fri 4pm PT) to walk through classifications and EPRs.

proc-bot: PRC-981 status update: classification assigned = Class B, next step: procurement review for budget alignment.

rafael: Thanks team. If you have an urgent question ping me or lauren directly. And please don't bypass ticketing for EPRs unless absolutely necessary (call first then file). :phone:

priya: filing a sample EPR to test flow, will delete after confirmation.

lauren: Governance note: any intentional misuse of EPR or misclassification to circumvent approval thresholds will be audited and may result in revocation of emergency privileges.

emma: Will the finance dashboard show EPR spend separately? would be helpful for monthly reporting.

rafael: Yes 1: EPRs will be tagged and visible in the monthly procurement report under "Emergency/Incident" bucket. We'll also export a list for exec review after month-close.
thread_summary: Procurement announces new consultant/vendor classification (Class A/B/C), intake link and templates, and an Emergency Procurement Request (EPR) fast-track process for security/incident-driven spend; includes GL codes, office hours, and governance notes.
